top_categories.workout_context: Battenkill's New York rolling hills gravel rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Battenkill's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
Battenkill's New York rolling hills, Rural gravel forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 63 miles.
At Battenkill, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Battenkill. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on New York rolling hills gravel, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Varied gradients on New York rolling hills gravel demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
63 miles on New York rolling hills gravel burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Battenkill, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
2-minute all-out efforts on New York rolling hills gravel. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Torque for headwinds and New York rolling hills gravel. When cadence drops below 70rpm, muscular strength keeps the watts up.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Battenkill’s 65 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
